the hypothesis, is an open decision for the project owner (roadmap

integrality of a smooth geometrically irreducible curve is a theorem

\begin{remark}
  \label{rem:JacobianWitness_smooth_redundancy}
  Smoothness is implied by smoothness of relative dimension \(g(C)\).  It is
  nevertheless useful to record both the abelian-variety property and the

\subsection{The Picard witness \(J=\Pic^0_{C/k}\)}
\label{sec:picardJacobianWitness}

\begin{theorem}[The Picard identity component is a Jacobian witness]
  \label{def:picardJacobianWitness}
  \uses{def:JacobianWitness, def:genus, thm:fga_pic_representability,
    thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety, thm:pic_zero_dimension_equals_genus,
    thm:albanese_universal_property_northstar}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.picardJacobianWitness}
  The identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) carries a Jacobian witness for
  \(C\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
  \uses{lem:curve_geometrically_integral, lem:curve_hypothesis_gap,
    lem:pic0_relative_dimension_genus, lem:pic0_isAlbanese_all_points}
  Representability of the relative Picard functor gives \(\Pic_{C/k}\), and its
  identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) is a group scheme, smooth, proper and
  geometrically irreducible by \cref{thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety}. Those four data
  are the first four fields of the witness; of the four,
  \cref{thm:pic0_smooth} and \cref{thm:pic0_proper} are the ones whose own proofs
  are still open.

  Three further steps are needed, and each is isolated as a lemma because it does
  not follow from the four above.

  First, the hypotheses must be reconciled: \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) is constructed for a
  geometrically \emph{integral} curve carrying a \(k\)-rational point, whereas a
  witness is required for every smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve.
  Geometric integrality is automatic (\cref{lem:curve_geometrically_integral}); the
  rational point is not, and is the single genuine gap
  (\cref{lem:curve_hypothesis_gap}), a gap only over a general base field ---
  over an algebraically closed field it is \cref{lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed}
  and the witness is \cref{def:picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed}.

  Second, the smoothness supplied by \cref{thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety} carries no
  relative dimension, while the witness records smoothness at the specific
  relative dimension \(g(C)\); the tangent-space identification
  \(T_0\Pic^0_{C/k}\cong H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)\) of
  \cref{thm:pic_zero_dimension_equals_genus} supplies the dimension, and
  \cref{lem:pic0_relative_dimension_genus} is the resulting refinement.

  Third, the Albanese structure is required for \emph{every} \(P\in C(k)\) and for
  every genus, whereas \cref{thm:albanese_universal_property_northstar} is proved
  over an algebraically closed base field and for \(g(C) > 0\); the extension is
  \cref{lem:pic0_isAlbanese_all_points}. Together these seven data form the
  required witness.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A smooth geometrically irreducible curve is geometrically integral]
==========
  \(k\)-rational point.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
  This assertion is \emph{false} as stated. A smooth proper geometrically
  integral curve need not have a \(k\)-rational point: a conic over \(\mathbb{Q}\)
  with no rational point is a genus-\(0\) example, and there are genus-\(2\)
  curves over \(\mathbb{Q}\) with no rational point. Over an algebraically closed
  field a rational point always exists, since a curve there is a nonempty
  Jacobson space whose closed points are rational.

  The lemma is therefore stated here only to name the gap between the hypotheses
  of the witness and those of the Picard construction, and it is not provable in
  this form. Closing it requires either weakening the claim --- carry
  \(C(k) \neq \emptyset\) as a hypothesis of the Jacobian itself, which proves
  something weaker than intended --- or replacing the input by a representability
  statement that needs no section, namely representability of the \'etale
  sheafification (\cref{sec:fga_pic_setup}). That choice is open. The algebraically
  closed case is not affected by it and is \cref{lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A curve over an algebraically closed field has a rational point]
  \label{lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed}
  \leanok
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.hasRationalPoint_of_curve_of_isAlgClosed}
  \uses{def:has_rational_point}
  Let \(C\) be a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over an algebraically
  closed field \(\bar k\). Then \(C\) has a \(\bar k\)-rational point.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  Geometric irreducibility over the one-point base \(\Spec \bar k\) makes the
  underlying space of \(C\) irreducible, in particular nonempty, and smoothness makes
  \(C \to \Spec \bar k\) locally of finite type, so that space is a Jacobson space.
